Voter Turnout in 2012 in the United States.

Source: R/data.R
full_turnout.Rd

County-level voter turnout data for counties in the United States in the 2012 presidential election at each of V3097 counties and independent cities in 2012. In this data set, a county's voter turnout is defined as the number of people who voted for a presidential candidate in that election divided by the number of citizens in that county who are at least the minimum voting age (18 years or older) multiplied by 100 (to convert to percent).

Usage

full_turnout

Format

An sf object with an NAD83 / Conus Albers point projection with 3097 rows and 12 columns:

  • county: the name of the Virginia county.

  • turnout_12: voter turnout (defined above, in percentage points) in the 2012 election.

  • median_hh_inc: the median household income (in thousands of dollars).

  • clf_unemploy_pct: the unemployment percentage (in percentage points).

  • lesscollege_pct: the percentage of the population with less education than a college degree (in percentage points).

  • age29andunder_pct: the percentage of the population that is aged 29 and under (in percentage points).

  • age65andolder_pct: the percentage of the population that is aged 65 and older (in percentage points).

  • female_pct: the percentage of the population that is female (in percentage points).

  • ruralurban_cc: a code for how "urban" the county is, defined as: 1 if the county has a metro area of 1 million or more people, 2 if 250,000 to 1 million, 3 if metro area has fewer than 250,000, 4 if county has 20,000 or more and is adjacent to a metro area, 5 if county has 20,000 or more and is not adjacent to a metro area, 6 if county has an urban population of 2500 to 19999 and is adjacent to a metro area, 7 if county has an urban population of 2500 to 19999 and is not adjacent to a metro area, 8 if county is completely rural or has less than 2500 of an urban population and is adjacent to a metro area, and 9 if county is rural or has less than 2500 of an urban population and is not adjacent to a metro area.

  • white_pct: the percentage of the population that is white (in percentage points).

  • rural_pct: the percentage of the population that lives in a rural area (in percentage points).

  • geometry: the point coordinates (centroids) of the county or city district.

Source

Data were obtained at https://github.com/MEDSL/2018-elections-unoffical/blob/master/election-context-2018.csv from the MIT Election Data and Science Lab and were subsequently supplemented with data from the United States census using the tidycensus R package.
